about.title: About Sleep Calculator - Sleep Cycle Reference
about.description: The Sleep Calculator estimates bedtime and wake-up times based on sleep-cycle timing assumptions. It can be used to review different sleep schedules and compare bedtime or wake-time options. Use the result as a general sleep-planning reference rather than a medical recommendation or a prediction of sleep quality.

faq.q: How much sleep do I need based on my age?
faq.a: Adults typically need 7-9 hours, teenagers 8-10 hours, and children 9-11 hours. Older adults (65+) may need 7-8 hours. Individual needs may vary based on lifestyle, health factors, and activity levels.

faq.q: What are sleep cycles and why do they matter?
faq.a: Sleep cycles are 90-minute periods consisting of light sleep, deep sleep, and REM sleep. Completing full cycles helps you wake up feeling refreshed rather than groggy. The calculator times your sleep to end at the completion of a cycle.

faq.q: Why do I feel groggy when I wake up?
faq.a: Waking up in the middle of a deep sleep phase can cause grogginess and sleep inertia. Try adjusting your bedtime to complete full 90-minute cycles, which allows you to wake up during lighter sleep phases.

faq.q: Should I keep the same sleep schedule on weekends?
faq.a: Yes, maintaining consistent sleep and wake times, even on weekends, helps regulate your circadian rhythm and improves overall sleep quality. 'Social jet lag' from irregular schedules can disrupt your natural sleep patterns.
